title: A timeline that 'looks better'
topic: Probity in records, forms and certification
stem:
You are an F2 doctor on a general medical ward. A family has complained that their mother, Mrs Ellis, waited too long to be reviewed after a fall on the ward last week. You reviewed her, but didn't write your note until two hours later.

Your registrar asks you to add a note to the record dated and timed at the time of the fall, "so the timeline looks better".
instruction: Choose the 3 most appropriate actions to take in this situation.

options.text: Add the note as asked, as you did review her.
options.brief: The note would still misrepresent when it was written.
options.detailed: You did review her, which makes this tempting. But the note would suggest it was written at the time, which isn't true.

options.text: Decline, explaining that you can't backdate an entry.
options.detailed: A note timed to look as though it was written earlier would misrepresent what happened, and could mislead the complaint investigation. Declining, politely, keeps the record honest.

options.text: Offer to add a clearly dated retrospective note giving any relevant detail.
options.brief: Late entries are acceptable when they are clearly labelled.
options.detailed: If you have useful information to add, such as when you actually reviewed her, you can write a new entry with today's date and time, making clear it is retrospective. That adds detail without misleading anyone.

options.text: Add the note without any date or time.
options.brief: Undated entries are poor practice and may also mislead.
options.detailed: This avoids backdating, but undated entries can be read as contemporaneous, and records must show when entries were made.

options.text: Tell the family that your registrar asked you to change the notes.
options.brief: Not the right route, and may inflame the complaint.
options.detailed: The family deserve an honest response, but this isn't the way to raise your concern. Speaking to your consultant is the right route.

options.text: Report your registrar to the GMC.
options.detailed: The request is a concern, but a single request you declined is best raised locally first.

options.text: Agree, but add a note elsewhere explaining that the entry was backdated.
options.detailed: This tries to balance honesty with the registrar's request, but the backdated entry itself would still be misleading.

options.text: Seek advice from your consultant or the trust's complaints team.
options.brief: Seniors can advise on responding to the complaint properly.
options.detailed: Your consultant or the complaints team can advise on how to contribute honestly to the response, including writing a statement about what happened.

explanation.issue: This tests whether you keep records honest when a senior asks you to change them to look better in a complaint.
explanation.keyDetails: You did review her, but wrote the note later. The record is relevant to a complaint. Your registrar is asking you to backdate.
explanation.reasoning: [B] declines, [C] offers an honest alternative, and [H] seeks advice. The distractors misrepresent the record ([A], [D], [G]), or handle the concern inappropriately ([E], [F]).
explanation.competing: [G] is the tempting distractor, as it seems to keep some honesty, but the backdated entry itself would still mislead.

references.title: Good medical practice
references.note: Domain 4, honesty in records; Domain 1, recording when entries are made.
